Static trace: prescan_vault_mints applies its unrecognized/danger-extension rejection only when either mint snapshot is writable. A read-only PermanentDelegate mint then falls through because holds_authority models only the base and transfer-fee authority fields. The pinned Token-2022 processor permits PermanentDelegate to authorize TransferChecked while the mint account remains read-only. TransferFee is expressly excluded from the unmodelable mask; WithdrawWithheldTokensFromAccounts likewise keeps the mint read-only and mutates source/destination token accounts, which conservation ignores when they are not vault-owned. A Warden-signed CPI can therefore exercise a dangerous authority without changing any compared mint field, repeating the instruction-scope and skipped-check prior-art classes despite the specification's unconditional 1B rejection requirement.

commitPresent returns false for every git cat-file failure, and line 180 continues without first attesting that the repository is shallow. Consequently, in a full clone a fabricated or mistyped valid-looking SHA is indistinguishable from unavailable shallow history and skips all path/name-at-SHA validation. The separate HEAD-side check verifies only the current file and test name, so it cannot establish that the cited historical artefact exists.

t22_native_account_delta_is_counted_in_sol_not_by_mint constructs both its token account and mint snapshot with production NATIVE_MINT_2022, while the classifier compares against that same constant. A typo therefore changes the implementation and synthetic input together, allowing the test to pass for a noncanonical address. every_danger_extension_sets_its_bit similarly constructs TLVs with the production EXT_* identifiers that the parser matches. The values at this head agree with the pinned Token-2022 source, so this is a defect in the lane's ability to detect future layout drift, not a demonstrated current identifier mismatch.
